- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or volatility, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., >+2% from prior), true outcome often corrects downward; apply “overshoot correction” by subtracting 1–2% from forecast 2–3 days later.  
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85–88), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per day to avoid overestimating near-term rally.
